title: claude-autoresume usage/scoped_limits.json
description:
The widget -> daemon relay of ACTIVE per-model usage caps (e.g. the weekly Fable limit), at ~/.claude-autoresume/usage/scoped_limits.json.

Why it exists: the daemon is pure-stdlib and cannot reach claude.ai, and a CLI transcript that hits a per-model cap records only a plain 429 (isApiErrorMessage / apiErrorStatus 429, model '<synthetic>') with NO reset time of its own - the reset lives solely on the usage page. The widget already fetches usage, so it drops the active caps here and the daemon arms a model-limited session against the relayed reset.

Concurrency: single writer (the widget's ScopedLimitLogger), single reader (the daemon). Written with Data.write(.atomic), i.e. auxiliary file + rename, so the reader sees either the old inode or the new one, never a partial file. No cross-process flock is needed or taken - unlike snapshots.jsonl, nothing else ever writes here.

Semantics: this file is a FULL-STATE snapshot rewritten on every usage fetch, not a log. An empty `limits` array is meaningful - it means a cap just reset and there is nothing to wait on.
x-in-band-version-note: No version field. `updated_at` is present but no reader consumes it, so the daemon has no staleness check on a relayed reset - see findings F5-3.
x-writers: ClaudeUsageOverlay ScopedLimitLogger.buildPayload (from UsageFetcher, every successful usage fetch)

updated_at.description: ISO8601 with offset, from Swift's ISO8601DateFormatter([.withInternetDateTime]) - when this relay was written. WRITE-ONLY: no reader consumes it.

limits.description: The currently-ACTIVE per-model caps only. The widget filters on isActive before writing, which is why the daemon's loader does no is_active filtering of its own - an invariant that is not representable in the file itself and must not be broken silently on either side.

scopedLimit.description: One active model-scoped cap. These field names are the WIDGET'S OWN relay format, frozen here independently of whatever the claude.ai API renames itself to - the typed values come from the ClaudeAPI module, which is the only place allowed to know raw API field names.

model_display_name.description: Human-facing model family name, e.g. 'Fable'. The daemon's primary match key: normalize_model_token folds this and a transcript model id onto the same family token ('claude-fable-5' <-> 'Fable').

model_id.description: Concrete model id when the API supplies one, else null. Used by the daemon only as a FALLBACK match key when model_display_name is empty.

resets_at.description: When this cap's window rolls. The whole point of the file: a limit whose reset is unparseable or null is skipped by the daemon's loader, so the model-limited session stays visible as 'waiting' but is not armed for auto-resume until a later relay supplies one. parse_reset_timestamp also normalizes stringified epoch-milliseconds, which an earlier bug parsed as year ~57000.

percent.description: How much of the cap is consumed. WRITE-ONLY: the daemon never reads it.

severity.description: The API's own severity label (e.g. 'critical'). WRITE-ONLY: the daemon never reads it.
